title: Finite-stage local module objects without transitions
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a functor with Noetherian rings $R_k$, and $c$ a limit cone of $R^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\operatorname{Spec}$ with affine vertex $S$. Fix $i\in I$ and a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, locally finitely presented morphism $f:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Put $X=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}S$ and $X_j=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$ for $j\geq i$ [def-pc-base-change]. For a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $M$ on $X$ [pqf-def-coherent], there are $j\geq i$, a finite affine open cover $U_a\to X_j$, and finitely presented quasi-coherent modules $N_a$ on $U_a$, each equipped after pullback to $X$ with an isomorphism to the restriction of $M$. No transition maps or compatibility between these isomorphisms are asserted.

source.place: Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR: First proof of Tag 01ZR, finite affine-cover object lifting; object clause of Tag 05N7

proof.text: Choose a finite affine open cover of Xi. The inverse images of each chart at finite stages and at the limit are affine; their coordinate rings are tensor base changes. Identify the limit chart ring with the directed colimit by identifying S with Spec(colim R), using uniqueness of limits and tensor-product pullback. Finite presentation and quasi-coherence of M give a finitely presented section module on each limit chart. The object clause of the affine module descent theorem supplies a finite-presentation stage model, realized as its associated module sheaf.

There are finitely many chart stages. Use directedness to choose a common upper bound also above i. Extend each stage module to that index and use composition of pullbacks to transport its comparison with M. Scalar extension preserves finite presentation; associated sheaves are quasi-coherent. Pull back the original finite cover to this stage. The transition maps of the ring system are affine, so these charts are still affine. For a preorder use the partial-order quotient of the nonempty upper tail. The empty source uses the empty family and zero section modules use zero presentations.
